component.name: OpenDoctrines
component.summary: Grand strategy: run a country and its neighbours

description.p: OpenDoctrines is a grand strategy game about running a country: its industry, its armies, its research, its politics and its neighbours.

Provinces have population, industry, fortification, resources and an ethnic composition. Countries have a treasury, a research programme, a political compass, claims on their neighbours and opinions about each other. Rebellions spawn from unrest and hold real territory, wars pull in guarantee chains, and ceasefires are negotiated over provinces, money and dropped claims.
Six historical scenarios on a 1641-province world map:

ul.li: Modern Day (2000) — 185 countries, populations from World Bank totals
The Powder Keg (1914) — five empires and a continent of alliances
The Last Spring (1918) — Germany has won in the east, and is losing in the west
Year Zero (1945) — the war is over and nothing has been settled

description.p: There is also a map editor with a procedural generator, host-authoritative multiplayer that needs no port forwarding, and a WebAssembly mod SDK with bindings for thirteen languages.
This is an alpha. It is playable and it is not finished — most notably there is no tutorial yet.

description.p: Reported bugs, three of which stopped people playing: sign-in on Windows, and two save faults.
Forty-four languages, and the twenty already there finished.
Plays inside Discord as an Activity; join a game with an invite code alone, through the account service's relay.
